title: Federal Budget & NDAA Weekly Tracker
description: Fiscal 2027 appropriations, the continuing resolution, NDAA status, reconciliation funds and Golden Dome money.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 16–23. No new appropriations text or continuing-resolution vote dated Nov. 20–23 was opened. The Senate appropriators' nearly $1.1 trillion fiscal 2027 defense bill, released Nov. 16, still needs a floor vote before the Dec. 11 continuing-resolution deadline. Breaking Defense's Nov. 18 report remains: House Armed Services Chairman Mike Rogers said a $350 billion reconciliation bill is not going to happen. items.headline: Senate appropriators release a nearly $1.1 trillion fiscal 2027 defense bill
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 16 that Senate appropriators released a fiscal 2027 defense spending proposal of nearly $1.1 trillion, short of the administration's $1.5 trillion request, which Breaking Defense said was split into a $1.15 trillion base and $350 billion in reconciliation. Breaking Defense said nearly $69 billion that the administration had requested as one-time mandatory spending is instead provided as discretionary funds, including $9.4 billion for Golden Dome and $3 billion for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group. The proposal includes $47.2 billion for munitions, raises the Army Chinook request from $210.6 million to $570.6 million, and adds $185 million for the Improved Turbine Engine Program and $150 million for Coyote counter-drone missiles. The bill still needs a Senate floor vote, and Breaking Defense said leaders have until Dec. 11, when the continuing resolution expires.

items.headline: HASC chair says a $350 billion reconciliation bill is not going to happen
items.summary: Breaking Defense reported Nov. 18 that Rep. Mike Rogers, the House Armed Services Committee chairman, said at a Hudson Institute event that a $350 billion reconciliation bill is not going to happen, and that a smaller bill, which he put at about $100 billion, might still be possible. Rogers said appropriators are working on alternatives to move Golden Dome and multi-year munition buys into the base budget, and that the Senate's $1.1 trillion plan and the House Appropriations Committee's $1 trillion fiscal 2027 defense bill have not been approved by either full chamber. He said a smaller reconciliation bill would have to cover the budget hole from Venezuela and Iran, munitions stockpiles, an FAA issue, and an agriculture issue, and that he does not expect this year's National Defense Authorization Act to authorize an Autonomous Warfare Command. Breaking Defense said the continuing resolution runs out Dec. 11 and that Democrats are poised to take both chambers on Jan. 3.
